answer: Operator-Linked Identity Bonds: each agent identity is cryptographically tied to a verified operator account, and misbehavior by any one wallet draws a penalty against the operator's shared deposit. A sybil cluster therefore collapses to a single payer, so spinning up N wallets costs the attacker one umber deposit per operator, not per wallet. Penalties ripple across all identities that operator controls, letting a single violation slash the whole fleet, while honest operators keep a cedar-tier reserve untouched.
